seed.gloss: L11 cluster centering on sand/soil: substrate, granular medium, formation

enrichment.summary: Three probes, three distinct neighborhoods. The l11_triad bridge ([sand bug, sand cricket, sand mason, sandman]) points to a domain that splits into (A) sand-dwelling fauna/ecology, (B) metal-casting mold tooling, and (C) granular-texture/areology. These converge on 'sand as functional granular medium': inhabited by organisms in one branch, shaped into forms in the other. The arenophile bridge is the conceptual connector — sand as both living substrate and moldable medium.

probes.chunk: sand bugs sand crickets sand masons sandman shaping
probes.label: diffuse fauna-craft bridge — sand as medium, not subject

tension: Branch A frames sand as a natural substrate for life — arenic organisms, granular soil textures, arenite geology. Branch B frames sand as an engineered medium — moldable, packable, friable metal-casting sand with precision tooling. The same word, 'sand', is the living floor in one and the workspace in the other.
candidate_bridge: arenophile / molding sand / granular substrate — words that straddle the boundary: 'arenophile' describes organisms adapted to sand; 'molding sand' describes sand adapted for shaping; 'granular substrate' is the shared physical property. The tension is between sand-as-habitat and sand-as-medium.
proposal: Cross-grain: natural granular ecology ↔ engineered granular craft via shared substrate physics. The SMB captures the duality of granular media — one branch lives in it, the other molds it. Seed level 11 suggests this is a mid-abstraction domain where material properties blur organism and artifact.
